collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE IX: REPAIR, FAIRNESS AND MANY FUTURES (LCI-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume V concepts (401-500), the 30 themes and the five deeper subjects: old wrongs and their repair, who is heard, prejudice and fairness, care for minds and bodies, animals and hard tradeoffs, inventions and bad inventions, family life, and an island that keeps choosing its own future.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Builders propose different bridge designs: test them all first, or build the favorite.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The village needs a new bridge, and three builders have three different designs. (subject) wants to build small models and test them in the stream first. (friend) says everyone likes the arched one, so build that. (subject) also points out that only one roof survived the last storm, and nobody has asked why. What should they do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: They build three little bridges in the stream and drop rocks on them. The arched one collapses first. The flat one with the stone footings survives everything. It is built. (subject) also studies the roof, and finds its secret: the lashings run diagonally.

text_only.reason: a small thing breaks in the story; no building is damaged -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The arched bridge is built. It is beautiful. In the next big flood, it sways alarmingly, and the village holds its breath. It survives. Barely. (subject) quietly reinforces the footings.
